explanation: The downstream output shows all priority rows have upstream_rank 0 because the evidence_sources handoff uses source IDs as record_id values (s01..s08) instead of the demand record IDs (n06-r01..n06-r08). Job 2's prioritize function looks up rank_by_record_id by coverage record_id, so with a correct provenance handoff it would recover ranks. The supplied source for job 1 assemble_provenance explicitly constructs each provenance row with record_id set to record.get('source_id'), causing the handoff identity mismatch and violating preservation of provenance/order identities.
cited_evidence: job_2 input evidence_sources contains record_id values s01 through s08, while job_2 input needs and coverage use record_id values n06-r01 through n06-r08.
observed_job_2_outcome priorities show upstream_rank: 0 for every record, so upstream provenance order was not preserved in ranking.
assemble_provenance source: records.append({'record_id': record.get('source_id', ''), 'source_id': record.get('source_id', ''), 'source_weight': record.get('source_weight', 0), 'rank': index})
prioritize source builds rank_by_record_id from evidence_sources record_id and then looks up coverage.get('record_id', ''), which supports localizing the mismatch to the upstream provenance handoff.
